sources.title: ART 2: self-organization of stable category recognition codes for analog input patterns
sources.access: NLM bibliographic record and author abstract

implemented: Paper describes a neural architecture for incremental category formation for analog and binary inputs; no quantitative experiment or executable implementation verified in this pass.
learned: Category codes formed or updated from input patterns.
designed: Comparison, matching and reset mechanisms and stability/plasticity regulation.
limit: Abstract-level access; no verified universal stability guarantee or evidence of generalized cognition.
ora: Historical comparator for preserving acquired distinctions while processing new experience; distinguish persistent new categories from unchanged input coding.

sources.access: NLM indexed record; subsequent direct page gave only footer; details of experiment not audited

sources.title: A real-world rational agent: unifying old and new AI

implemented: 2003 article reports comparison of modified DAC, prior DAC and another control in simulated and physical robot foraging, with reported improved task performance.
learned: Acquisition of experience-dependent information supporting behavior, within designed control mechanisms; exact learning variables and experimental details await audit.
designed: Foraging environment, task definition, robot sensors/actions and control structures; Bayesian-equivalent modification authored.
limit: Author-reported improvement not independent reproduction; no claim of endogenous goals or unlimited competence. 1998 record limited.
ora: Relevant precedent for task-specific comparative controls in embodied behavior, and for checking whether a measured improvement is attributable to a specific mechanism.

sources.title: Why Neurons Have Thousands of Synapses, a Theory of Sequence Memory in Neocortex
sources.access: NLM abstract and Numenta author project paper page

sources.authors: Yuwei Cui; Subutai Ahmad; Jeff Hawkins
sources.title: Continuous Online Sequence Learning with an Unsupervised Neural Network Model

implemented: Author group reports streaming sequence prediction comparisons against statistical and recurrent neural baselines using synthetic and real data. Claimed comparable accuracy, not uniformly superior performance.
learned: Temporal associations, context-dependent predictions, simultaneous candidate predictions.
designed: Sparse representation, neuron architecture, encoding interfaces and synaptic update rule.
limit: Same research lineage; biological universality remains a hypothesis. Prediction tasks do not establish independent goal formation or open-ended development; full comparative protocol unreviewed.
ora: Distinguish learned temporal regularities from innate reactions, and compare against simple history-based predictors before making a cognition claim.
rights: Bibliographic identifiers and original analysis only. No full texts or source tables redistributed; publication rights not assumed.

sources.authors: Randall C. O'Reilly; Michael J. Frank
sources.title: Making working memory work: a computational model of learning in the prefrontal cortex and basal ganglia
sources.access: NLM abstract; related research lineage, not a separate validation of all LEABRA claims

implemented: 1996 thesis reports network simulations combining associative and error-driven learning; related 2006 model reports learned gating in working-memory tasks.
learned: Connection weights and representations; in related actor-critic model, task-relevant gating policies.
designed: Neural topology, inhibitory regulation, error/target or reinforcement signals and learning rules.
limit: Local learning signals do not establish that the objective is endogenous or that real cortex uses the precise algorithm; transfer results not audited at methods level.
ora: Distinguish local computation from independence of externally supplied objectives; distinguish acquired memory control from having memory alone.

sources.authors: Stan Franklin; Tamas Madl; Sidney D'Mello; Javier Snaider
sources.title: LIDA: A Systems-level Architecture for Cognition, Emotion, and Learning
sources.access: author manuscript page 1 image and sections II, V–VII, X–XI excerpts; full methods audit pending

funding_acknowledgement.qualifier: Named author support in first-page footnote; not proof each award funded the entire architecture

implemented: Authors report agents simulating reaction time and attention phenomena; explicitly distinguish conceptual LIDA from implemented LIDA. Attentional blink reproduction reported.
learned: Episodic learning reported implemented in framework; procedural learning in predecessor but not integrated then. Article states neither learning form had been validated against human data at that time; perceptual learning remained in progress.
designed: Attention, memory interfaces, action selection; some task-specific nodes and schemes explicitly supplied. Much of affect and higher-level cognition still conceptual.
limit: 2014 snapshot only; functional access-consciousness terminology not a claim of subjective experience. Behavioral fit is not evidence of acquired task knowledge. No full methods review.
ora: Especially useful evidence that conceptual module names and empirical behavior must be audited separately. Do not use apparent attention or emotion as proof of learning or feeling.
rights: Bibliographic identifiers and original analysis only. No full texts or source tables redistributed; publication rights not assumed.

sources.title: Machine Psychology: integrating operant conditioning with the non-axiomatic reasoning system for advancing artificial general intelligence research
sources.access: publisher full HTML accessed; abstract, sections 7–8 selected methods and results examined; no comprehensive E2 audit

implemented: OpenNARS for Applications (ONA) configured for sensorimotor reasoning only. Article reports discrimination, reversal, and conditional discrimination experiments, with no-feedback test blocks. Simple and conditional discrimination tests reported perfect performance on three 12-trial blocks.
learned: Evidence-dependent action preferences and temporal hypotheses updated by feedback, including reversal.
designed: Explicit symbolic stimuli, two supplied actions, designer-set goal, feedback encoding, learning rules and timing.
limit: No declarative inference rules enabled in this configuration; limited symbolic task domain and explicit goal signal. Reported task accuracy not an independent reproduction or proof of unrestricted grounding. Foundational Wang thesis is a separate pending lead.
ora: Relevant conceptual benchmark for behavioral adaptation after contingencies change and retention when training feedback is withheld. Does not authorize installing or running NARS or changing Ora.
rights: Bibliographic identifiers and original analysis only. No full texts or source tables redistributed; publication rights not assumed.

sources.authors: Chris Eliasmith; Terrence C. Stewart; Xuan Choo; Trevor Bekolay; Travis DeWolf; Yichuan Tang; Daniel Rasmussen
sources.title: A Large-Scale Model of the Functioning Brain
sources.access: public article copy, first article page image and limitation excerpt; https://library.scottbarrykaufman.com/uploads/2012/12/Eliasmith-et-al.-2012.pdf ; supplement and correction unreviewed

implemented: Spaun instance of semantic pointer architecture: 2.5 million simulated spiking neurons; same constructed model presented with eight prescribed task types, input images and simulated arm output.
learned: Within-task reward-based weight changes in a selected reinforcement learning task; no acquisition of wholly new tasks in original model.
designed: Neural subsystems, task cue vocabulary, representations, action selection and visual/motor interfaces.
limit: Authors explicitly report lack of developmental account, inability to acquire entirely new tasks, fixed attention/eye position and restricted representations. Original article correction noted in cover sheet but contents not retrieved; supplements pending.
ora: Large scale and multi-task performance are insufficient evidence of self-developed cognition. A strong historical example of separating engineered function from acquired ability.
rights: Bibliographic identifiers and original analysis only. No full texts or source tables redistributed; publication rights not assumed.
